summary.text: Survival analysis is a branch of statistics for analyzing the expected time until one event occurs, such as death in organisms or failure in mechanical systems.
It asks what proportion survive past a certain time, at what rate survivors fail, and how circumstances or characteristics raise or lower the chance of survival.
It copes with censoring, where a subject's exact survival time is unknown, and uses the survival function S(t), the probability of surviving longer than time t.

facts.label: Other names
facts.value: Reliability engineering, duration analysis, event history analysis

facts.label: Survival function
facts.value: S(t) is the probability of surviving longer than t

facts.label: Censoring
facts.value: Some information is known, but not the exact survival time

facts.label: At time zero
facts.value: 100% of subjects are alive without an event

facts.label: Reading the plot
facts.value: A vertical drop is an event; a tick is a censored subject

items.prompt: A patient in a drug study is followed for 13 weeks with no relapse, then moves away and cannot be reached. How is this patient recorded?

options.label: As having had an event at 13 weeks
As a censored observation
As having survived forever
As a mistake to be removed

items.explain: Censoring means some information about survival time is known but not the exact time, such as a subject lost to follow up.

items.prompt: In a study, the survival function at 10 weeks reads 0.8. What does that mean?

options.label: 80% of subjects had an event at exactly week 10
The study lasted 80 weeks
The chance of surviving longer than 10 weeks is 0.8
Eight subjects were censored by week 10

items.explain: S(t) is the probability that a subject survives longer than time t.

items.prompt: You draw a survival curve. At the very start of observation, what proportion of subjects is still alive without an event?

options.label: None of them
Half of them
Only the censored ones
All of them

items.explain: At time zero, 100% of the subjects are alive without an event.

items.prompt: An engineer studies how long machines run before failing, using the same mathematics as a medical study of patients. What is her field called?

options.label: Reliability engineering
Event history analysis in sociology
Duration modelling in economics
Clinical trial design

items.explain: Survival analysis is called reliability theory, analysis or engineering in engineering.

items.prompt: On a survival plot, you see a sudden vertical drop at 8 weeks and a small tick mark at 45 weeks. What do they show?

options.label: A censored subject at 8 weeks and an event at 45 weeks
Two events, one at each time point
An event at 8 weeks and a censored subject at 45 weeks
Two censored subjects at those weeks

items.explain: A vertical drop indicates an event, and a vertical tick mark indicates that a subject was censored at that time.

items.prompt: Why can it be harder to define the 'event' for a mechanical system than for a living organism?

options.label: Machines cannot be observed over time at all
Machines never fail in any real sense
Machine failure may be partial or a matter of degree
Organisms never die at a specific time

items.explain: Biological death is unambiguous, but mechanical failure may be partial, a matter of degree, or not localized in time.
